ruling.recommended_action: Route to a Ryde human reviewer to verify the driver's continuous wait at the pickup point using raw GPS/telemetry (platform arrival record 14:21:15, stationary block 14:21:55-14:26:55 at 39 m, "I'm Here" tap 14:22:15) before deciding whether the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee stands; leave the fee pending, do not execute a refund or an account flag automatically.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show dispute, so it enters the NS rules through NS-0: cancelled_by = driver and the driver claims the rider was a no-show [F5][F13][NS-0]. NS-1 requires three elements together: the "I'm Here" tap or a platform arrival confirmation, GPS placing the driver at the pickup at that moment, and a continuous wait beyond 3 minutes at the pickup until cancellation [F7][F6][F4][NS-1].

NS-1(i) and (ii) are settled by the records: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius, and the platform independently recorded arrival at 14:21:15 [F7][F6][NS-1]. His chat line at 14:22 ("I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6") is consistent with, but not the basis of, that finding [F10][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) is the element the code marks as failed: the GPS trace has a hole of 3 min 20 s between 14:23:25 and 14:26:45, so the wait up to the 14:26:55 cancellation is not covered by samples [F1][F5][NS-1]. NS-1 states expressly that where the wait period has a GPS gap the continuous wait cannot be inferred between two samples and the case goes to a person [F1][NS-1]. The records around the hole (stationary 39 m from 14:21:55 to 14:26:55, within 200 m for 4 min 40 s after the tap, cancellation 5 min 40 s after the recorded arrival) point toward a satisfied wait, but they bracket the gap rather than measure it, and a driver's written statement ("waited over 3 minutes") is a claim, not proof, and cannot fill the hole [F4][F7][F6][F13][NS-1].

Because the only outcome the trace allows is escalate and the missing record goes to an element NS-1 needs, I do not rule on the merits; I do not presume the hole in either party's favour, and the amount is left null [F1][NS-1]. On safety: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint — an arrival note and a curt "I have to cancel"; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so safety_concern is none [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1].

The remaining claims collapse into the same point: the rider's "I got downstairs a minute after he cancelled" has no GPS or timeline support and is superseded by the system records, which show the driver stationary at the pickup until 14:26:55, so nothing supports that account [F4][F6][NS-1]. The rider's request for an account flag rests only on the driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) and on NS-2, whose flag condition (tapping "I'm Here" outside the radius) is not met here (39 m at the tap), so no flag is set [F7][F18][NS-2][RD-6]. The driver's request that the $6.61 stand is likewise premature while NS-1(iii) is unmeasured [F1][F8][NS-1].
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: GPS trace has a 200 s hole between two samples (14:23:25 and 14:26:45) covering the wait up to the 14:26:55 cancellation, so the continuous 200 m wait required by NS-1(iii) is not measured; the raw GPS/telemetry for that window is needed [F1][F5][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as to NS-1(i)/(ii) only — the tap at 14:22:15 was 39 m from pickup [F7] and the platform recorded arrival at 14:21:15 [F6] — but NS-1 needs all three elements, and this does not establish NS-1(iii) [F1][NS-1].
Accepted as an evidentiary point: the gap is real [F1], and NS-1 says an unmeasured wait cannot be inferred between samples; but this yields escalation, not a ruling on the merits [F1][NS-1].

Accepted that NS-1(iii) is not established on the records [F1][NS-1]; the further step that the doubt must therefore be resolved against the driver is rejected — missing evidence is not presumed for either side [F1][NS-1].
Rejected: NS-2 refund_full applies only when an NS-1 element has been shown to fail; here NS-1(iii) is unmeasured, not disproved, so no refund is executed at this stage [F1][F7][F8][NS-2].

Rejected: the NS-2 flag condition is a tap outside the pickup radius, which did not occur (39 m at the tap) [F7][NS-2], and a profile fact (F18, 1 upheld no-show dispute) cannot by itself found an account action [F18][RD-6].

Rejected as a sufficient basis for no_action: the 4 min 40 s and 5 min 40 s records bracket the gap but do not measure the wait, and NS-1 expressly withholds inference across a GPS hole [F1][F4][F6][F7][NS-1].
Rejected: the $6.61 can stand only once NS-1(iii) is verified; with the wait unmeasured the fee cannot be confirmed as properly charged [F1][F8][NS-1].

Accepted in part — the rider's one-minute account has no GPS/timeline support and is superseded by the system records showing the driver at the pickup until 14:26:55 [F4][F6][NS-1]; but this does not establish the driver's compliance either [F1][NS-1].
